items.title: John E. Wood Interview, 1986-06-26
items.q: actually Greg Stafford who ended up giving me a ride from that, where that parade ended up, back down to the French market where he was late playing his gig at the Cafe Mediterranean.

ctx.x: Well, it's just, it's a different sound and you wouldn't expect it to be a sound.

No, it's a different, you know, it's, actually Greg Stafford who ended up giving me a ride from that, where that parade ended up, back down to the French market where he was late playing his gig at the Cafe Mediterranean. And I got into that because he had seen me before the parade started talking to, to Barry Ratton. And he had overheard some things that, that Ratton was saying to me, I guess was in response to a question I had asked him about the band that I had heard him play with the week before. And, you…

But it's the same tradition. That's basically what he was saying. And I have no real argument with that. You don't want it to be just an antique replica of something else. It's got to be something that's his and of the present. But he was very conscious, and he could articulate that concept, I thought, very well.
